ops.title: Codex generated-handler review: framework callback attribution regression in codex.4
ops.body:
Independent review: generated-handler identity

Verdict: FINDINGS. One new regression remains in the frozen codex.4 source and wheel; the earlier source and installed-matrix PASS messages are superseded by this report.
Task task_bfb3a16b91f9; dispatch ctx_8b688b6db6e3.
Captain Hook checkout: /Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/captain-hook/galeocerdo.
Monorepo checkout: /Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/monorepo/codex-monorepo.
Reviewer made no source edits; all probes and test copies are under /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity.

Open finding: P2 — preserve framework-owned hook attribution

Location: captain_hook/app.py:248#m8hx. The conditional treats every handler defined anywhere inside the framework as an authored generated hook. It therefore rebinds framework-owned loader callbacks as well as nudge/gate primitives. captain_hook/loader.py:149#cvzz and :168#y219 register internal SessionStart callbacks through on; their source changes from loader.py to the first external stack frame. When the CLI registers them, that frame is Click decorators.py.

The CLI intentionally omits non-pack framework hooks by checking whether source_file lies inside package_root at captain_hook/cli.py:630#ddqe. With the patch, announce_faults, announce_pr_status, and provision_pack_resources appear as three extra local hooks. This is a runtime attribution regression, not a test-order-only failure: tests/test_cli.py:83#rptt's exact-sorted-row test passes alone on the baseline and fails alone on the exact installed codex.4 wheel. Logs: /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-cli-baseline-a.log and /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-cli-wheel-a.log.

The effect extends to internal hook state identity. An independent probe invokes the same register_pr_announcements through two external caller filenames. Baseline stores loader.py and the same announce_pr_status.60a38dbec78c key both times; codex.4 stores the two caller filenames and produces announce_pr_status.cfbfaaa5a8b9 versus announce_pr_status.39c368967285. Because announce_pr_status has max_fires=1, registration through a different caller can select a separate counter. Evidence: /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-internal-baseline.log and /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-internal-wheel.log; script internal_callbacks.py under the review directory.

Recommendation: narrow author-callsite attribution to authored primitive-generated registrations while retaining definition-file attribution for framework-owned loader callbacks. Preserve the existing caller helpers and public on API; do not relax the CLI exact-row expectation to bless extra local framework hooks. Add a regression proving both the CLI rows and internal callback source/key remain unchanged across invoking filenames. The source owner owns the fix; a runtime correction requires a new immutable wheel version rather than replacing codex.4. Findings were sent directly to the owner and coordinator in msg_e9a35d259220 and msg_d50859bfd774 before completion.

The separate full-suite empty-project-discovery failure was reported by the coordinator; that identity test passes in the independent focused suites below. Its order-dependent cause remains with the source owner and was not diagnosed by this review. The confirmed isolated CLI failure is sufficient to withhold acceptance.

Baseline and resolved finding

The original on registration stored fn.__code__.co_filename. A gate delegates to nudge, whose generated handler lives in captain_hook/primitives/nudge.py. Discovery stamps a project or pack root, but RegisteredHook._state_identity cannot relativize that library file against the author root and therefore uses its absolute path (captain_hook/types.py:1069#fevp). Existing caller_file and framework_frame already distinguish internal framework files from builtin pack author files (captain_hook/state.py:270#atvr and :292#bph7).

Two independent baseline library copies reproduced the unstable generated keys across project .claude/hooks, project .capt-hook/hooks, two named packs, and a builtin pack. Each case had an ordinary on handler plus gate and nudge: the direct handler remained stable while both generated keys changed with the library root. Evidence: /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-baseline.log and baseline-matrix.json under the review directory.

The first implementation unconditionally captured caller_file for every handler. I reproduced a regression: a normal function defined in separate_author.py and registered from a different file acquired the registration file instead of retaining its definition file. The failed snapshot app.py SHA256 was a0bbd5175c91e4445d312660673ad56ba400443cc777cd19de914f9c7f7fa81f; evidence /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-wip.log. The owner corrected this before source acceptance.

Reviewed source

app.py SHA256: 9d1b8ef832ec32d5de5a9fe45d192915d8f265b06f1de4675f3da4e946ceb9ee.
The change captures the registration author at captain_hook/app.py:228#amt5, then chooses that author only when framework_frame classifies the function definition as framework code at :248#m8hx. Otherwise fn.__code__.co_filename remains authoritative. The existing predicate excludes builtin_packs, so normal builtin decorators retain their own files while generated builtin handlers resolve to the builtin author. No public signature, handler object, hook name, caller traversal algorithm, discovery API, or state-key algorithm changed.

Independent source verification

- Review matrix: two separate library roots, five placements each, thirty registrations total, and Claude plus Codex behavior checks for every registration. Project and pack generated identities now equal identity.py or pack-name plus NUL plus identity.py; direct hooks and imported normal functions retain definition attribution. Returned decorator identity, on signature, hook names, registration fields, native adapter outputs, and nudge max_fires behavior match the baseline. Log /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-source.log; structured source-matrix.json and source-app.diff under the review directory.
- Isolated focused pytest: test_app.py, test_pack_imports.py, test_nudge.py, test_state.py, and test_decisions_writer.py: 169 passed in 1.75 seconds. Log /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-tests.log. These ran against immutable package copies, not the owner's working checkout.
- Owner regressions examined: tests/test_pack_imports.py:119#hvf0 (library relocation), :152#yky7 (both project hosts), :168#s0fb (builtin attribution), and the ordinary/imported handler case. The live decision-writer expectation now names the author test file. Historical rows containing primitive-library paths were not rewritten.
- ccx vcs diff recorded in /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-source-diff.txt; scoped git diff --check passed.

Monorepo constraints

The gate remains byte-identical to HEAD:.claude/hooks/rebase_on_dev_before_pr.py and to the pre-review moved candidate: SHA256 74031c65c3809b9a67067558f6cb234e259b96b8c3aec6730ce3ddd97069081d. The test file changes only the expected generated key from rebase_on_dev_before_pr:gate_ce4d91a7.0efbf6949c62 to rebase_on_dev_before_pr:gate_ce4d91a7.84a6d4e48926. The new suffix is SHA256(rebase_on_dev_before_pr.py)[:12], independently calculated. The rollout manifest /tmp/codex-port-monorepo-rollout.json matches both the unchanged gate and updated test bytes; test SHA256 ccfa8fed56245d2bdfeae719ecfacd2f3a7c71742b751953adbad376895d0dcd. No gate policy was weakened to satisfy the identity expectation.

Compatibility limit

Generated hooks move once from the old installation-dependent key to the stable author-relative key. Existing per-hook state stored under the old key is not migrated or read through a compatibility alias; a capped generated hook can therefore fire again after this upgrade within an existing session. Ordinary user on keys remain unchanged. Later library or project/pack installation moves preserve the new discovery-stamped key. Ad-hoc registrations without a discovery root still use the existing absolute-path fallback; this patch does not promise stability for those registrations or redefine hook names when author files move.

Installed wheel verification

Artifact: /tmp/codex-port-dist/capt_hook-12.51.0+codex.4-py3-none-any.whl.
SHA256: 0bcc01b97fec89b874e9d5bc4705a90f09cbb080f5b34f4e834c28785e95cd0f.
The embedded app.py and both installed copies match the reviewed app.py SHA256 above. Installed metadata reports capt-hook 12.51.0+codex.4. The runtime dependency environment was /tmp/codex-port-final-downstream-venv/bin/python, with cc-transcript 14.19.0+codex.6; no shared environment was modified. Each library installation used uv pip install --no-deps --target /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity/wheel-{a,b} with the exact wheel.

- HOOK_REVIEW_PYTHON=/tmp/codex-port-final-downstream-venv/bin/python /tmp/codex-port-final-downstream-venv/bin/python /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity/run_matrix.py wheel: PASS. Ten relocation cases, thirty registrations, both native adapters per registration, with baseline-equivalent names, API signature, registration fields, outputs, and nudge fire limit. Log /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-wheel-matrix.log; structured wheel-matrix.json under the review directory.
- Same interpreter selection, run_counters.py wheel: PASS. Separate processes load nudge from different library and author roots but share session state. On both hosts the first call warns and the second returns no result under the identical counter:nudge_c780b88e.e0e9c9078ced key. The baseline run warns twice under two different keys. Logs /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-wheel-counters.log and /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-baseline-counters.log.
- Exact wheel-b package, pytest tests/test_app.py tests/test_pack_imports.py tests/test_nudge.py tests/test_state.py tests/test_decisions_writer.py -p no:cacheprovider: 169 passed in 1.93 seconds. Log /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-wheel-tests.log.
- Exact wheel-b package, pytest tests/test_review_fix.py -k 'resolve_target or real_misfire_complaint' -p no:cacheprovider: 9 passed, 99 deselected. Historical primitive-path attribution still works. Log /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-wheel-legacy.log.
- Pytest ran from /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity/test-source with PYTHONPATH naming wheel-b and that test snapshot. The checkout site-packages directory was appended after the staged interpreter paths to supply pytest_asyncio and test-only dependencies. The earlier checkout-only environment's missing ToolUseBlock.origin failure reproduced identically before and after this patch; the staged dependency run resolved it. No dependency fallback was added to product code.
- PYTHONPATH=/tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity/wheel-a PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /tmp/codex-port-final-downstream-venv/bin/python /Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/monorepo/codex-monorepo/.capt-hook/tests/test_hosts.py -v: all 6 methods pass. This includes all 91 inline cases across Claude, Codex function-call history, and Codex completion history: 273 native policy replays, independently counted. Log /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-monorepo.log.
- Final signature/name/behavior equivalence, installed source hashes, and replay count: /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-final-validation.log.

The reviewer did not run broad make, change global installations, commit code, or spawn workers. The coordinator reported a broader make failure still under diagnosis when handing over this wheel; this scoped identity PASS does not resolve that separate build gate. The initial source/matrix passes were sent before the isolated CLI regression was found; the later FINDING messages explicitly supersede them. The artifact remains the owner's immutable codex.4 wheel.
